style:
STYLE (non-negotiable): the first attached image is the approved target painting. Match its exact pigments, value range and hand: dry matte medieval fresco, broad deliberate brush masses, iron red, burnt umber, dirty limestone ochre, charcoal, restrained ash ivory, visible chipped plaster. Coarse shapes that read at game resolution, not micro detail. This is one surface of one building, so its colours must sit next to that painting without any seam. No photoreal rendering, no gloss, no airbrush, no lens blur, no text, no letters, no invented occult symbols.

Paint the surface evenly and neutrally lit, with no cast shadows or vignette and no perspective: light in the game is added later. Dark values may appear only where the paint itself is dark.

bay-a.tool: Codex image_gen through codex exec, reasoning effort high
bay-a.prompt:
Portrait 2:3 image. Paint one flat, perfectly straight-on wall elevation of a side bay of the chapel. No perspective at all.

The second attached image is an exact layout template, and its shapes are real 3D geometry in the game. Keep every boundary exactly where it is drawn, to the pixel: the two pointed niches, the narrow colonnette between them, the large pointed tympanum above, and the red dado at the bottom. Fill the whole frame edge to edge.

Contents: inside each pointed niche, a tall screaming damned figure in a tattered shroud with raised bony hands and a long black open mouth, painted on dark red plaster. Inside the tympanum, a crowded group of three or four huge screaming figures with reaching hands on iron red, exactly the kind of figures on the side walls of the target painting. Around them, worn limestone blocks with thin red and ivory painted bands following the arch edges, large patches of chipped plaster.
